To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

substituting the raw gradient with its momentumized version in adaptive gradient methods can well improve optimization and generalization, which is backed up by both empirical evidence and theoretical analysis.

substituting the raw gradient in the second momentum estimation term with its momentumized version can well solve the issue of gradient-based adaptive methods that they tend to be trapped at local minima at a very early stage during training and thus generalize worse than SGD.

substituting the second moment estimation with that of the momentumized gradients in Adam improves the performance of optimization and generalization, which can be explained by the fact that momentumized gradients contain more accurate directional information.
